Step 3: Understanding check

Why do the DC motors need a motor driver instead of being connected directly to the Arduino output pins?

Safety: never connect a motor battery directly to Arduino I/O pins. Match the real motor driver's voltage, current, grounding and power connections to its datasheet before building hardware.

Block-based programming

Choose the robot's action for each branch of the control algorithm.

WHEN ROBOT STARTS → REPEAT FOREVER
IF distance ≤ 20 cm
ELSE
END IF → REPEAT

Try the default logic, then change the sensor distance.

Arduino C++ editor

Edit the threshold and the two motor actions. Check & simulate recognizes only this starter-code pattern; it is not an Arduino compiler.

Use the starter sketch. Hardware wiring and motor power must be checked before uploading to a real robot.

Robot safety challenge

Configure the program to stop at or below 20 cm and move forward when the path is clear. Test three scenarios.

Knowledge check

Why do we divide the ultrasonic echo time by 2?

Educational model: idealized HC-SR04 timing at 343 m/s. The arena uses a custom perspective 3D renderer; it is not a physics engine. The automatic avoidance path is an instructional state-machine approximation. Designed for classroom demonstrations.

Obstacle course challenge

Use the arrow keys or the controls to navigate the robot from START to GOAL without hitting obstacles. The ultrasonic range indicator estimates the nearest obstacle ahead. This is a simplified top-down navigation exercise.

Reach the green goal. Turning does not move the robot.

Student worksheet: Obstacle-Avoiding Robot

1. Label the Arduino Uno, HC-SR04, L298N, motors and battery.

2. Why must the ultrasonic echo time be divided by two?

3. Write pseudocode to stop the robot when distance is at most 20 cm.

4. Explain why a motor driver is needed.

5. Propose one improvement to the robot's obstacle avoidance.
